external_entities.name: colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague who signs in through the identity broker and uses applications.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.

external_entities.name: franchise colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague from a franchise store who signs in through their own identity provider.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.

external_entities.name: identity provider
external_entities.description: The identity provider used by franchise colleagues to vouch for their sign-in.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: The system that supplies group membership changes and leaver information to the identity broker overnight.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Group membership is not maintained there by hand — it comes from the HR system overnight.

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: The broker signs colleagues in, issues tokens, accepts federated sign-ins, and provides public keys for token verification.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: An application that allows a holder of a token containing the store-manager group to change prices and void transactions for every store.
processes.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.

processes.name: application
processes.description: An application that takes the broker-issued token and uses its groups to decide what the colleague may do.
processes.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: A store containing the signing key used by the identity broker to sign tokens.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory containing colleagues and the groups they are in.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: A log to which the broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what that log records, whether it covers the franchise route, or whether the directory or the log are encrypted where they sit.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: A colleague signs in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: A franchise colleague signs in through the identity broker using a federated identity.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.

data_flows.name: vouch for sign-in
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for a franchise colleague's sign-in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them

data_flows.name: change prices
data_flows.description: A colleague uses the store admin console to change prices and void transactions when their token contains the store-manager group.
data_flows.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.
data_flows.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.
data_flows.data_description: store-manager token, price changes, and transaction voids

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: An application fetches the public half of the broker's signing key from the broker to check token signatures.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.data_description: public half of the token-signing key

data_flows.name: read signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker uses the signing key kept in the key store to sign tokens.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_flows.name: maintain directory
data_flows.description: The identity broker maintains and uses the directory of colleagues and groups.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: pull changes
data_flows.description: The identity broker pulls group membership and leaver changes from the HR system once a night.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night, and that is also how leavers stop being colleagues.
data_flows.data_description: overnight group membership and leaver changes

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-in events to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network on which the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: colleagues home devices
trust_boundaries.description: The home devices from which colleagues may sign in to the identity broker.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

trust_boundaries.name: franchise stores
trust_boundaries.description: The franchise environment containing franchise colleagues and their own identity provider.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

assumptions.assumption: The identity broker is internally exposed because the text says it runs on the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The broker is described as running on the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The store admin console is internally exposed because the text says it runs on the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The store admin console is described as running on the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The store admin console presents a web interface because it is described as a console.
assumptions.basis: The text calls it the store admin console; console is treated as a web application interface.

assumptions.assumption: The key store is confidential because it contains the signing key used to sign tokens.
assumptions.basis: The store contains a signing key, which is a secret.

assumptions.assumption: The directory is confidential because it contains colleagues and their group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The directory contains colleague identity information and group memberships.

assumptions.assumption: The HR system is in the corporate network boundary because it supplies internal colleague and leaver information to the broker.
assumptions.basis: The HR system is described as the source of internal group membership and leaver changes; its network location is not stated.
